chapters.summary: Jesus Christ is God the Word made flesh; John the Baptist bears witness to him, and Jesus calls his first disciples to follow him.
keyPoints: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and all things were made through him.
John the Baptist bears witness of the Light so that people might believe through him, though he himself was not that Light.
Jesus calls Andrew, Peter, and others, who recognize him as the Messiah and follow him.
chapters.application: Let us meditate each day on Jesus as the light of life, live out his love in our daily lives, and boldly bear witness of him to others, pointing to Christ with the same humility as John.

chapters.summary: Jesus performs his first miracle at the wedding in Cana, turning water into wine to reveal his glory, and cleanses the temple, foreshadowing the arrival of a new age.
keyPoints: Jesus attends a wedding at Cana with his disciples, and when the wine runs out, his mother tells him.
Jesus instructs the servants to fill six stone waterpots with water, and when it is drawn out, it has become good wine.
Jesus goes up to Jerusalem and drives out those buying and selling in the temple, declaring that his Father's house must not be made a house of merchandise.
chapters.application: In the everyday lack and hardship we face, let us trust Jesus' provision, for he can turn what is ordinary into abundance; at the same time, let us examine our own hearts and worship God in spirit and in truth.

chapters.summary: Jesus speaks with Nicodemus about being born again, making clear that God so loved the world that whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, while whoever does not believe stands condemned already.
keyPoints: A person must be born of water and of the Spirit in order to see the kingdom of God.
God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes should not perish.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already.
chapters.application: Let us respond each day in faith to God's love, be renewed in life by the Spirit, live out the testimony of new birth, and share this good news of salvation with those around us.

chapters.summary: Jesus speaks with the woman at the well in Samaria, revealing living water and worship in spirit, and leads many Samaritans to believe in him.
keyPoints: Jesus speaks with the Samaritan woman about living water, exposes her past, and leads her to recognize the Messiah.
Jesus teaches that true worship of the Father is not confined to a mountain or to Jerusalem, but must be in spirit and in truth.
Many Samaritans believe in Jesus because of his own word, and testify that he is the Saviour of the world.
chapters.application: Let us be like that woman - laying down our past, receiving the living water Jesus gives, worshipping him in truth in our daily lives, and sharing the gospel with those around us.

chapters.summary: Jesus heals a paralyzed man at the pool of Bethesda and explains his relationship with the Father, revealing that he is Lord of life and judge of all.
keyPoints: Jesus heals on the Sabbath a man who had been paralyzed for thirty-eight years, provoking the hostility of the Jews.
Jesus declares that he works together with the Father, doing what the Father does, giving life and executing judgment.
Jesus points to the witnesses of who he is - John the Baptist, the Father, and the scriptures - and rebukes the Jews for not believing what Moses wrote.
themes: The Son's Relationship with the Father
chapters.application: In the midst of our busyness, let us stop to listen to the Lord's voice, believe that he is the source of life, and find in him true rest and hope.

chapters.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish, and teaches the crowd that he is the bread of life, so that whoever believes in him has eternal life.
keyPoints: Jesus feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, revealing his power and might.
The crowd seeks Jesus only for food, but he directs them to seek the food that endures unto eternal life.
Jesus declares that he himself is the bread of life, and that whoever believes in him will never hunger and will never thirst.
chapters.application: Do not labor for the food that perishes, but seek the bread of life. Read God's word and pray each day, trust in Jesus, and find satisfaction and eternal life.

chapters.summary: Jesus goes up to Jerusalem during the Feast of Tabernacles, teaches publicly, and declares that he is the source of living water, stirring up varied opinions and division over who he is.
keyPoints: Because of the hostility of the Jewish leaders, Jesus chooses to go up to Jerusalem for the feast secretly.
Jesus teaches openly in the temple, and the people marvel at his learning, as he points out the true meaning of the law and the Sabbath.
Jesus declares that whoever believes in him will have rivers of living water flowing out of him, referring to the Spirit, which stirs up debate and division.
themes: The Choice Between Belief and Unbelief
chapters.application: When we face doubt and conflict, let us come before Jesus, for he is the fountain of living water, able to satisfy the deep thirst of our hearts and give us peace and guidance.

chapters.summary: Jesus forgives a woman caught in adultery, and declares that he is the light of the world, debating truth and freedom with the Jews.
keyPoints: Jesus forgives the woman caught in adultery, and urges her to sin no more.
Jesus declares that he is the light of the world, and that whoever follows him will have the light of life.
Jesus teaches that the truth will set people free, and debates with the Jews over what it means to be children of Abraham.
chapters.application: When we are caught in wrongdoing, Jesus does not condemn us, but offers us the chance of new life. Let us receive his light, walk in the truth, and enjoy true freedom.

chapters.summary: Jesus heals a man born blind, and the Pharisees question him over healing on the Sabbath, ultimately revealing spiritual blindness alongside the true identity of Jesus.
keyPoints: Jesus opens the eyes of a blind man using spittle and clay, showing that God's work is not bound by convention.
The Pharisees interrogate the blind man and his parents, yet refuse to acknowledge that Jesus comes from God.
The healed man boldly testifies of Jesus, and comes to believe that he is the Son of God.
chapters.application: When our lives are transformed by the Lord, let us boldly testify to his work, and not shrink back because of others' doubts. May the Lord open the eyes of our hearts, that we may truly know him.

chapters.summary: Through the parable of the good shepherd, Jesus reveals the love that lays down his life to save the sheep, and declares that he and the Father are one, granting eternal life to those who believe.
keyPoints: Jesus is the door of the sheep, and whoever enters by him will be saved.
The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep, while the thief comes only to steal and kill.
The Father has given the sheep to Jesus, and no one is able to pluck them out of his hand.
chapters.application: When we feel lost or afraid in life, let us remember that Jesus is the good shepherd - he knows us, watches over us, and gives us the assurance of eternal life, so that we may live in peace and guidance.

chapters.summary: Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead, revealing that he is the Lord of resurrection and life, which in turn stirs up the hostility of the religious leaders.
keyPoints: Lazarus is gravely ill, and Martha and Mary send word to Jesus, but Jesus deliberately delays before going to them.
By the time Jesus arrives at Bethany, Lazarus has already been dead four days; Jesus weeps at the tomb and calls Lazarus to come forth, raising him to life.
Many of the Jews believe in Jesus because of this, but the chief priests and Pharisees plot together to kill him.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us believe that Jesus' delay is not refusal, but is meant to accomplish something greater. He is the Lord of resurrection, able to give hope in the midst of despair.

chapters.summary: Jesus is anointed at Bethany, enters Jerusalem in triumph, and foretells that he will be lifted up to draw all people to himself.
keyPoints: Mary anoints the Lord with costly ointment, while Judas complains about the cost, revealing two very different hearts.
Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey as the crowds cry out 'Hosanna,' while the Pharisees mutter among themselves.
Jesus declares that the hour has come, comparing himself to a grain of wheat that must fall into the ground and die in order to bear much fruit.
chapters.application: May we follow Mary's example, offering our very best to the Lord; and may we, like Jesus, be willing to lay down our lives, becoming a blessing to many.

chapters.summary: At the Last Supper, Jesus washes his disciples' feet, teaching them to serve one another in humility, and foretells that Judas will betray him.
keyPoints: Jesus washes his disciples' feet, setting an example of humble service.
Jesus points out that Judas will betray him, fulfilling what the Scripture had said.
Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another, just as he has loved us.
chapters.application: Let us follow Jesus' example of humility, willingly serving others, loving our brothers and sisters with the love of Christ, and living out unity and witness in the church.

chapters.summary: Jesus comforts his disciples, promises to send the Holy Spirit, and teaches them to trust in him and keep his commandments.
keyPoints: Jesus goes to prepare a place for his disciples and promises to come again and receive them into the Father's house.
Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through him.
Jesus promises to send the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, who will dwell within believers.
chapters.application: In times of worry, let us remember that Jesus has already gone to prepare an eternal home for us, and has given us the Holy Spirit to help us at all times. Let us trust in him, and our hearts need not be troubled.

chapters.summary: Using the image of the vine and the branches, Jesus teaches that his disciples must remain united to him, and instructs them to love one another and to expect persecution for his name's sake.
keyPoints: Jesus is the true vine and the Father is the husbandman, who cuts away every branch that bears no fruit.
Whoever abides in Jesus, letting his words abide in them, will have their prayers answered and will bear much fruit to the Father's glory.
Jesus commands his disciples to love one another as he has loved them, and warns them that the world will hate them.
chapters.application: Today, let us remain in Christ, staying connected to him through Scripture and prayer, letting love flow out in our daily lives, and bearing good fruit to the glory of God.

chapters.summary: Jesus warns his disciples of coming persecution, promises to send the Holy Spirit as the Comforter, and explains his going away and returning, and how the disciples' sorrow will be turned into joy.
keyPoints: Jesus warns his disciples that they will face persecution, but reminds them that he has already overcome the world.
The Holy Spirit will come to guide the disciples into all truth and to glorify Christ.

Jesus explains that his departure is for the disciples' good, since the Comforter will not come unless he goes; their present sorrow will turn to joy, like a woman's pain in childbirth, and that joy no one will take from them.
chapters.application: Sorrow and hardship are unavoidable in life, but the Spirit is with us, and Jesus has overcome the world. Let us look to Christ in our difficulties, with hearts at peace, for his promises never change.

chapters.summary: Before his departure, Jesus prays to the Father, asking for glory, unity, and protection for himself, his disciples, and all future believers.
keyPoints: Jesus prays that the Father would glorify him, so that he in turn may glorify the Father, having finished the work the Father gave him to do.
Jesus prays for his disciples, asking the Father to keep them from the evil one and to sanctify them through the truth.
Jesus prays for future believers, that they may be one, just as the Father and the Son are one.
chapters.application: Let us follow Jesus' example, caring for others in prayer, pursuing unity with our brothers and sisters, and trusting firmly that the Father will keep us to the end.

chapters.summary: Jesus is arrested in the garden of Gethsemane, brought before Annas and Caiaphas for questioning, denied three times by Peter, and finally handed over to Pilate.
keyPoints: Jesus steps forward to face those who come to arrest him, and secures the safety of his disciples.
In the courtyard, Peter denies Jesus three times, fulfilling what Jesus had foretold.
Jesus is questioned before both the Jewish and Roman authorities, declaring that his kingdom is not of this world.
chapters.application: When circumstances are hard, we may be as weak as Peter. But Jesus already knew our weakness, and still loved us to the end. May we be strengthened in the Lord, and never deny his name under trial.

chapters.summary: Jesus is scourged and crowned with thorns, condemned by Pilate, and crucified; on the cross he completes his work of redemption, and afterward is buried by Joseph and Nicodemus.
keyPoints: Pilate has Jesus scourged, and the soldiers mock him, placing a crown of thorns on his head.
Though Pilate can find no fault in him, he yields to the pressure of the Jews and hands Jesus over to be crucified.
On the cross Jesus says, 'It is finished,' and gives up his spirit; his body is laid in a new tomb.
chapters.application: Meditate on what Jesus suffered for you, receive his salvation with a thankful heart, and let your life follow his example of obedience and love, living out the self-giving spirit of the cross.

chapters.summary: John chapter 20 records the risen Jesus appearing to his disciples, strengthening their faith and sending them out to proclaim the gospel.
keyPoints: On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene finds the stone rolled away from the tomb and runs to tell Peter and John.
Peter and John see the empty tomb and the linen cloths, and believe that Jesus has risen, though they do not yet understand the Scriptures.
Jesus appears first to Mary, then to his disciples, giving them the Holy Spirit, and Thomas believes because he has seen.
chapters.application: May we, like the disciples, seek the Lord even in our doubt, be filled with peace at the sight of the risen Lord, and boldly proclaim this good news.

chapters.summary: Jesus appears to his disciples for the third time by the Sea of Tiberias, restores Peter, and foretells his future.
keyPoints: The disciples fish all night and catch nothing, until Jesus directs them and their net is filled with a great catch.
Jesus prepares breakfast for his disciples and asks Peter three times whether he loves him.
Jesus foretells that Peter will die a martyr's death, and stresses the importance of following him.
chapters.application: Whatever our failures or confusion, the Lord takes the initiative to seek us out and restore us in love. May we respond to his love, follow him steadfastly, and serve him faithfully.
